validity.recommendation: Real, correctly classified, single-owner project. Not a duplicate of P4449/P4450 (see cross_row_leads) -- P4449 (parent) is the conversion of the pre-existing Wet Header gathering system, P4450 is the sibling Rogers City Connector, and P4451/this row is the Norwalk Manistee Connector -- three distinct scopes under one MPSC certificate (Case No. U-20894). Caveat: independent sources confirm the combined ~6 route-miles of new pipe for the two connectors together (matching GEM's 2+4=6 mi split) but no accessible document breaks out NMC's individual 4.0 mi length or 12-in diameter, so those two cells remain UNRESOLVED at the segment level (see fills).
validity.researcher_notes: Checked the Manistee News Advocate article, the MPSC's own 2021-07-27 press release, the actual Commission Order in Case No. U-20894 (mi-psc.my.site.com), a later Proposal for Decision from a 2024 DMLC rate case (Case No. U-21525) with sworn cross-examined testimony, and the EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook (project key 'rogers city and norwalk manistee connectors|dte michigan lateral', tracked docket U-20894). All agree: DTE Michigan Lateral Company (DMLC), a certificated intrastate pipeline company, was authorized in July 2021 to convert its existing wet-gas-gathering Wet Header System to regulated dry gas transmission service and to construct two NEW connector pipelines -- the $7M Rogers City Connector (P4450) and the $13.9M Norwalk Manistee Connector (this row, P4451) -- serving Manistee, Traverse City, Alpena and Rogers City. This is real, existing infrastructure, not a GEM-only entity.

Testimony also states construction, planned for 2021, actually began in 2022 (matching the sheet's StartYear1=2022, which is really the construction-start year, not the in-service year).

cross_row_leads.facts: Rogers City Connector (RCC): $7M estimated cost (order + press release); same MPSC Case No. U-20894 certificate as this row; EIA workbook 'rogers city and norwalk manistee connectors|dte michigan lateral' (docket U-20894) shows the SAME status history as P4451: Approved 2021-10..2024-07 releases, then Completed from 2024-10 on, completed_date 2023-02-15, year_in_service_date 2023, combined cost $28M. The Case No. U-21525 PFD (adms.apps.lara.state.mi.us/Mpsc/ViewProposalForDecisionsDocument/340) states the combined actual cost of RCC+NMC came in $7.45M below the combined estimate. The same Status/StartYear1/ConstructionYear correction proposed for P4451 (operating / 2023-02 / construction began 2022) applies to P4450 -- route to that shard.

P4449 (parent row, every spec blank) likely represents the base-certificate scope of Case No. U-20894: DMLC's CONVERSION of its pre-existing, already-built Wet Header wet-gas-gathering system to regulated dry gas transmission service. The order is explicit that this conversion uses EXISTING pipe ('the majority of the route for new service ... limits new disturbances to the environment, with only approximately six miles of new pipeline to be constructed specifically for the RCC and the NMC') -- i.e. only the two connectors (P4450, P4451) involve new construction; the conversion itself adds no new physical pipe. If P4449 is meant to record that conversion scope, standing rule 'expansion with no new physical pipe -> LengthKnown=0, Diameter blank' should apply rather than leaving it fully blank/undifferentiated from its children -- recommend the orchestrator adjudicate P4449 against this order's 'Conversion of Existing Facilities' section (not itself researched in this shard).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The sheet's LastUpdated (2022-10) predates the pipeline's actual completion. Sworn testimony from DMLC's VP of Storage Assets in MPSC Case No. U-21525 (a 2023 rate case, PFD signed 2024-10-02) states 'the pipeline project became available for service on February 15, 2023,' and construction, though planned for 2021, 'began in 2022.' The EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook independently corroborates from its 2024-10 release onward: status 'Completed', completed_date 2023-02-15, year_in_service_date 2023, for the same docket (U-20894). Two genuinely independent sources (a Michigan Public Service Commission evidentiary proceeding and a federal EIA statistical survey) agree on the same date -- high confidence. Recommend Status -> operating, StartYear1 -> 2023 / StartMonth1 -> 2, ConstructionYear -> 2022. The same change applies to sibling P4450 (see cross_row_leads).

summary: P4451 (DTE Michigan Lateral / Norwalk Manistee Connector) is real and correctly attributed to DTE Michigan Lateral Co (100%); MPSC Case No. U-20894 + a 2024 rate-case PFD + EIA show it went into service 2023-02-15 (construction began 2022) -- Status should change from proposed to operating (StartYear1 2023), not a duplicate of P4449/P4450. Length (4.0 mi) and Diameter (12 in) remain UNRESOLVED -- only a combined 6-mi total for both connectors is publicly documented, no per-connector breakdown found; Capacity, Pressure and FuelSource also UNRESOLVED (not disclosed anywhere).
